mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% within a month signals a loosening of monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity in the market and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% within two months signals economic weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% within two months signals a contraction in supply, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 7% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in the same month, it signals a significant labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 7% and PAYEMS decreases > 100,000 in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) increase by more than 10% and real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter, it signals strong economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases > 10% and GDPC1 grows > 2% QoQ
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of the triggered instances despite the signal.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) increases by more than 3% year-over-year and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1%, it signals a strong supply-side expansion with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the triggered instances despite the signal.
